verdict.summary: Any Wrike user, including on the Free plan, can register an OAuth app in the App Console and any other Wrike user can authorize it straight away; the docs describe no review or marketplace gate. The main things to handle are 1-hour access tokens with rotating refresh tokens, a per-user data-center host (US or EU) returned with the token, and a 400 requests/minute limit.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create the app with + App, add an https redirect (https://localhost allowed), run the code flow. A permanent token from the console works for even faster single-user testing.

timeToProd.assumes: An OAuth app requesting wsReadOnly or wsReadWrite to read and write a user's tasks and folders; no listing in Wrike's integrations directory.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Neither the OAuth guide nor the help article mentions an approval step; the absence of review is our reading.

prerequisites.item: A Wrike account on a plan with the API tab (Free, Team, Business, Pinnacle, Apex or legacy equivalents)
prerequisites.why: Apps are created under Apps & Integrations > API, which is available on these plans.

prerequisites.item: 'Access to App Console (API Apps)' permission on your user type
prerequisites.why: Admins control this per user type; it's on by default for admins. Account owners always have the required API permissions.
Redirect URIs must follow OAuth 2.0 rules and use HTTPS; https://localhost is allowed for development.

scopeTiers.impact: Read tasks, folders, projects and comments as the user. Tokens inherit the user's own permissions.

steps.title: Sign in and open the App Console
steps.detail: In Wrike go to profile > Apps & Integrations > API, or open the App Console directly.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The console URL redirected to login.wrike.com/login on 2026-10-20; we didn't sign in.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Click + App, enter name, logo and description, add redirect URIs, and copy the Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://login.wrike.com/oauth2/authorize/v4?client_id=...&response_type=code&redirect_uri=...&state=...&scope=Default,wsReadOnly. Exchange the code (valid 10 minutes) with POST https://login.wrike.com/oauth2/token, grant_type=authorization_code.

steps.title: Store the per-user host
steps.detail: Save the host from the token response (e.g. www.wrike.com or app-eu.wrike.com) and call https://<host>/api/v4. The wrong base URL returns 401 not_authorized.

steps.title: Handle refresh-token rotation
steps.detail: Access tokens last one hour. Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token; each refresh returns a new refresh token and invalidates the old one, so persist it atomically.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The guide is inconsistent on whether to refresh against login.wrike.com or the host URL.

steps.title: Add rate-limit handling and batching
steps.detail: Back off on 429 too_many_requests (400 requests/minute per IP or token) and rate_limit_exceeded; use batch operations to cut call volume.

steps.title: Optionally connect via the hosted MCP server
steps.detail: Point an MCP client at https://mcp.wrike.com/v2 (Streamable HTTP). Older /app/mcp/stream and /app/mcp/sse URLs are v1. You still register your own OAuth app and add the client's redirect URL.

steps.title: Test with a second Wrike account
steps.detail: Authorize from a different Wrike account (ideally on an EU account too) to confirm cross-account and host handling.

agentCanDo: Implement the code flow, state checking and token exchange
Persist rotating refresh tokens and the per-user host
Pick minimal scopes per endpoint from the API reference
Configure an MCP client for https://mcp.wrike.com/v2
humanMustDo: Sign in and create the app in the App Console
Copy and store the client secret
Generate a permanent token for testing if wanted (needs a password, not SSO-only)
Customer side: admins may audit apps via App Activity (Pinnacle/Apex)

blockers.symptom: 401 not_authorized right after a successful token exchange
blockers.cause: Calling www.wrike.com when the user's data lives in another data center.
blockers.fix: Use the host value from the token response as the API base URL.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails with an invalid refresh token
blockers.cause: Wrike rotates refresh tokens; the old one is invalid after a refresh.
blockers.fix: Always store the newest refresh token and avoid concurrent refreshes.

blockers.symptom: 429 too_many_requests: 'IP or access token exceeded limit: 400 requests per minute'
blockers.cause: Exceeding 400 requests/minute per IP or token.
blockers.fix: Throttle per token, back off, and use batch operations.

blockers.symptom: Tokens suddenly stop working for a user
blockers.cause: Tokens are revoked when the user revokes access, resets their password or is deactivated, or when an admin uses 'Log in as this user' or changes password policy.
blockers.fix: Detect 401s and prompt the user to reconnect.

blockers.cause: License or quota limits on the customer's plan.
blockers.fix: Check the user's plan and degrade gracefully.

blockers.symptom: Can't find the API tab or create an app
blockers.cause: Your user type lacks 'Access to App Console (API Apps)'.
blockers.fix: Ask an account admin to enable it under Settings > User types.

nuances.text: Access tokens last one hour, authorization codes 10 minutes; permanent tokens never expire and grant access to all the user's data, so keep them to testing.
Tokens always inherit the authorizing user's permissions; scopes can only narrow access on certain endpoints.
Scopes are comma-separated and case-sensitive. There's no single scopes page: each API method lists the scopes it accepts.
Wrike's hosted MCP v2 server advertises only wsReadWrite, so an MCP-based agent can't request read-only access there.
Apps registered on developers.wrike.com (rather than the in-product API tab) need a support request before they can be configured.
On Pinnacle and Apex, customer admins see every API app used in their account (creator, authorized users, last OAuth activity) via App Activity.
